judgment.rationale: Unlike ordinary zoom jitter, this report gives a recording-dependent loss of both zoom and annotation that recovers only when recording stops; keep it distinct from #51481 until reproduced.
evidence: PowerToys 0.102.3101 on Windows 11 build 26300, running elevated; a diagnostic ZIP is already attached.
Start recording with Ctrl+5, repeatedly use Ctrl+1 or Ctrl+2, and eventually both operations stop responding until recording is stopped.
Current Zoomit.cpp has separate ZOOM_HOTKEY, DRAW_HOTKEY and RECORD_HOTKEY registrations and global recording/session state; VideoRecordingSession owns asynchronous capture lifecycle.
No PR directly referencing #52139 was found. The supplied sequence is enough for maintainer testing; the exact stuck state or timer/hotkey conflict is not established.
judgment.recommended_action: Exercise repeated zoom/draw transitions during an active recording and inspect the first state transition that stops accepting those hotkeys.

reproduce.title: Verify reported ZoomIt behavior
prerequisites: Use a Windows system supported by the tested PowerToys version.
steps: Start a full-screen recording with Ctrl+5.
Repeatedly enter and leave zoom using Ctrl+1, then repeat draw entry/exit using Ctrl+2 and Escape.
If zoom/draw stops responding, keep the recording active long enough to inspect hotkey dispatch and zoom/draw state, then stop recording.
Confirm whether zoom/draw immediately works again; repeat with a nonrecording control.
reproduce.expected_result: Zoom and annotation remain usable throughout recording and after it stops.
